newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Vestel targets $400 mln 1997 turnover.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Vestel targets $400 mln 1997 turnover.

text.p: Turkey's leading TV set and computer monitor producer Vestel Elektronik Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. plans to increase its turnover by 60 percent to $400 million in 1997, a senior company official said.
"We want to increase 1997 turnover to $400 million from $250 million in 1996," general manager Kazim Ulker told Reuters in an interview in the western town of Manisa.

The company targets to increase its production by about 100 percent in 1997 and produce two million TV sets and one million computer monitors. Ulker said Vestel would export more than 70 percent of the total output.
Vestel shares opened at 39,500 lira on Wednesday on the Istanbul stock exchange and closed the first session at 39,000 lira.

Vestel almost doubled its TV set production to one million units in 1996 from 567,000 in 1995. The company raised its output capacity to two million sets last year with a $25 million investment from one million.
Ulker said Vestel would spend $20 million for modernisation and new technology investments in 1997.
Vestel aims to increase its exports by 87.5 percent to $300 million in 1997 from $160 million last year.
About 85 to 90 percent of its exports consists of the products which it produces as an original equipment manufacturer (OEM).
"We make our exports for North America, the European Union (EU), some other European countries and far-east countries," he said.
Vestel signed an agreement with French supermarkets chain Carrefour to produce TV sets to be sold in Carrefour stores around the world.
Ulker said European TV sets producers began to prefer Turkey as a production base. "Because, Turkey is closer to the market and signed a customs union accord with the EU," he added.

The company's research and development department is studying new models, like built-in satellite receivers or picture-in-picture TV sets. "We do not receive any patent or licence from any foreign or domestic company," Ulker said.
The Vestel group entered into the Turkish white-goods market in early 1996 and plans to start investment in 1997 for domestic production.
Vestel reported 15.05 trillion lira turnover in the first nine months of 1996 against 4.29 trillion lira in the same 1995 period.
The company's net profit soared to 1.27 trillion lira from 135 billion lira.
